tagline: The oldest collective investment trust, delivering long-term capital and income growth since 1868
hero_kpi_rationale: Net asset value (NAV) total return is the principal performance indicator for an investment trust like FCIT, reflecting genuine portfolio growth. It is the fundamental driver of long-term shareholder value creation.

kpis.name: NAV total return
kpis.explanation: Total trust performance based on net asset value, including dividends and capital gains.
kpis.description: NAV total return reached +11.3% in 2023, versus +15.1% for the FTSE All-World benchmark.
kpis.signal: Solid performance underperforming benchmark (FTSE All-World +15.1%) due to underweight exposure to largest growth stocks.

kpis.name: Share price total return
kpis.explanation: Total shareholder return, including dividends and share price appreciation.
kpis.description: Share price generated total return of +8.1%, impacted by widening discount to NAV, moving from 3.0% to 5.9%.
kpis.signal: Negative impact from widening share price discount relative to NAV.

kpis.name: Dividend growth
kpis.explanation: Annual increase in dividends paid to shareholders.
kpis.description: Total dividend for 2023 was 14.7 pence per share, up 8.9% from 2022, representing the 53rd consecutive annual increase.
kpis.signal: 53rd consecutive annual dividend increase, demonstrating exceptional long-term stability and commitment to shareholders.

kpis.name: Ongoing charges
kpis.explanation: Annual cost of managing the trust expressed as a percentage of assets.
kpis.description: Ongoing charges fell to 0.49% in 2023, down from 0.54% in 2022, a reduction of 5 basis points.
kpis.signal: Fee reduction achieved through revised arrangement with Columbia Threadneedle and new JPMorgan US large cap growth mandate.

kpis.name: Net revenue return per share
kpis.explanation: Net revenue generated per share after fees, basis for dividend payments.
kpis.description: Net revenue return per share increased 13.7% to 15.83 pence, up from 13.92 pence in 2022, supporting dividend growth.
kpis.signal: Robust underlying income growth supporting continued dividend increases, despite inflationary pressures.

kpis.name: Capital reserves
kpis.explanation: Amount of capital reserves available for future investments or distributions.
kpis.description: Capital reserves stood at £4.66 billion as of December 31, 2023.
kpis.signal: Strong financial position with substantial capital reserves providing flexibility for future shareholder distributions.

kpis.name: Revenue reserve
kpis.explanation: Reserve funded by revenue surpluses to smooth dividend payments.
kpis.description: Revenue reserve stood at £107.3 million, covering nearly one full year of dividend payments.
kpis.signal: Revenue reserve covers nearly one full year of dividend payments, supporting dividend sustainability.

kpis.name: Gearing level
kpis.explanation: Use of borrowings to amplify investment returns.
kpis.description: Effective gearing stood at 9.9% at year-end (versus 7.3% at year-start), with total borrowings of £581.0 million at blended fixed rate of 2.4%.
kpis.signal: Effective gearing increased to 9.9% from 7.3%, well positioned with long-term borrowings at 2.4% blended rate maturing to 2061.

risks.title: Critical dependence on Columbia Threadneedle as sole manager
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned in second rank in Principal Risks section, with language emphasizing structural dependence ('Business Model is based on the premise of an effective and strong working relationship'). Trend improving after successful Aladdin integration, but residual uncertainty from BMO GAM/Columbia Threadneedle merger. Key person/supplier category with high weight for an externally-managed investment trust.

risks.title: Risk of loss of portfolio manager Paul Niven
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly named in 'Loss of Key Person' section as 'the person posing the largest key person risk', with nearly 10 years tenure. Language is measured ('confident that those people could be replaced') but nominal dependence is rare in filings and signals genuine concentration. Risk stable according to Board.

risks.title: Cyber threats and failure of outsourced IT service providers
risks.score_rationale: Categorized as 'unchanged' risk with explicitly maintained 'high' level ('risk of loss remains high, Board and management vigilance also remains heightened'). Strong language and central position in principal risks. Dependence on externalized third parties (custodian, IT vendors) amplifies exposure surface.

risks.title: Underperformance from asset allocation and inadequate stock selection
risks.score_rationale: First risk listed in Principal Risks, with language covering allocation, sector selection, gearing and derivatives. Board explicitly notes increase in this risk ('The Board considers that this risk has increased'), notably linked to AI. High weight as directly related to competitive value proposition of the fund.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks impacting diversified international portfolios
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in Investment Performance as aggravating factor ('geo political factors such as those described above'), referencing market shocks comparable to Covid-19. Internationally diversified portfolio with exposure to emerging markets and restrictive government controls. Trend stable but degraded global context.

risks.title: Technology disruption from artificial intelligence in the sector
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly identified as aggravated emerging risk ('The Board considers that this risk has increased'), with dual opportunity/threat formulation. New to Board communication for 2023, signaling recent awareness. Technology category with transversal impact on asset management.

risks.title: Transition to net zero carbon and ESG regulatory risks
risks.score_rationale: Classified as 'Emerging Risk' with formal commitment to carbon neutrality by 2050. Evolving language ('field that is evolving rapidly') and recognition of potential long-term performance impact. Trend stable but rising regulatory pressure on ESG disclosure (TCFD, SFDR) strengthens materiality.

risks.title: Competition and threat to closed-end fund model viability
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in Long Term Viability section as stress test factor ('potential threat from competition'), alongside regulatory changes. Although treated briefly, presence in ten-year stress tests indicates structural Board concern. Competitive pressure from passive ETFs and low-cost open-ended funds.

ai_positioning.summary: FCIT is not a direct technology player in AI, but its portfolio includes significant positions in leading AI companies such as Nvidia, Microsoft and Amazon. The trust therefore benefits from market enthusiasm for AI through investments in the 'Magnificent Seven'.
evidence: Portfolio includes Amazon, Apple, Microsoft and Nvidia
2023 gains were influenced by optimism around AI
Chairman explicitly mentions AI as performance driver
